heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 for image generation and Seedance 1.5 Pro for video generation — advanced ByteDance foundation models for premium visual production.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a cinematic full-bleed dark hero with an oversized abstract product render centered slightly right, layered glass panels, and a dominant logo proof band across the lower fold. Keep the composition unexpected by placing the headline and CTA in a narrow left-side column while the visual field expands across the rest of the canvas. Add radial-glow accents, subtle grid lines, and floating prompt/result frames to signal multimodal AI capability. Brand color must stay anchored in orange for CTA, chip highlights, and UI accents; avoid blue entirely. The hero should feel premium, technically credible, and production-ready, with strong contrast and a clear path into the video gallery section below.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a full-bleed cinematic hero to preserve ad continuity and immediately answer what the product is.
Use a logo-first trust band instead of a generic metrics block because the visitor temperature is warm and proof type is logos.
Shift into a visually immersive 3-step how-it-works section to satisfy the warm-traffic sequence early.
Alternate dark and light surfaces between adjacent sections to avoid monotony and keep the page feeling premium.
Present products as alternating spotlight modules rather than a generic feature list so image and video stories feel distinct.
Use a carousel for testimonials because there are 4+ quotes and the section should not become a dense wall of text.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 & Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Seedream 4.5 for high-quality AI image generation and Seedance 1.5 Pro for AI video generation with audio. See logos, how it works, product capabilities, pricing, and testimonials.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark cinematic field with orange radial glow, layered glass panels, floating prompt-to-result frames, and enterprise proof chips embedded near the CTA
sections.designNote: Hero must be content-first but visually dominant: headline explains this is AI image and video generation, subheadline identifies it for creative directors and production teams, and the CTA is a single solid orange button labeled Get started. Include a compact benefit list beneath the copy and avoid secondary CTAs. Use one strong product visual showing both image and video outputs to make the page feel premium and production-ready.

Make trust highly visible early: a horizontal logo marquee with 3-6 recognizable enterprise or creative logos, paired with a short credibility line. Keep this section lightweight and immediate, serving as the first proof layer after the hero. Use logos as the dominant trust signal rather than claims.

Insert the warm-traffic how-it-works sequence here as a 3-step, under-60-seconds flow. Use three asymmetric cards with a strong visual header, minimal copy, and one full-width CTA at the end of the section labeled Get started. The rhythm should feel faster and more practical than the hero, showing prompt input, generation, and refinement/output. Make this section bright and highly scannable to break the dark hero mood.

Reinforce credibility with a concise proof strip immediately after how-it-works. Since proof type is logos, reuse logos only if needed in a tighter endorsement band; otherwise pair the logos with a short enterprise-ready statement. This section should be darker again to restore cinematic tension and keep the sequence from feeling generic.

featurePresentation.primaryFeatureTitle: Seedream 4.5 for high-fidelity image creation and editing

sections.designNote: This is the main explanatory section and should not feel like a generic SaaS feature list. Use alternating product blocks: first a spotlight for Seedream 4.5 with a large preview panel and a 2-column supporting grid for the most important capabilities, then a second immersive block for Seedance 1.5 Pro with a richer video gallery treatment. Since there are 5+ features per product, the spotlight-plus-grid format is the right decision. Keep adjacent blocks visually different: Seedream can be white/light with crisp utility framing, while Seedance should switch to a dark, cinematic gallery style with motion emphasis.

Place pricing after the products so the visitor understands value before cost. Use two comparison cards or a side-by-side table for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Keep the language enterprise-oriented and avoid clutter. Every pricing CTA must still be Get started, with the primary button in solid orange at 100% opacity. On mobile, buttons must be full-width.

Use a testimonial carousel because there are 4+ testimonials and the content is role-diverse. Highlight creative director, video producer, and art director quotes first to match the audience. The styling should be editorial but compact, with one featured quote at a time and supporting dots or arrows. This section should feel credible rather than emotionally heavy.

End with a focused conversion block that prefers seeing it in action over sign-up language, but the only button label must remain Get started. Keep the final CTA visually dominant: solid orange, large, full-width on mobile, and surrounded by minimal copy. Use a floating glass card over the dark background to close with strong contrast and urgency without becoming aggressive.

blueprint.designPersonality: High-end creative technology with a cinematic, production-studio feel: dark, intelligent, and enterprise-trustworthy, with orange as the unmistakable brand anchor and logo proof as the dominant trust mechanism.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a premium abstract product render for the hero: floating AI output frames, cinematic thumbnail strips, waveform accents, and layered prompt-to-result visuals. For the second fold, build an enriched video gallery with multiple autoplay-style preview tiles, playback scrubber shells, audio-wave overlays, and story-driven thumbnails showing motion, lip-sync, and camera movement. Use PNG for UI/product mockups and JPEG for the hero visual field. Keep iconography crisp and minimal in SVG.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and needs a slightly reduced but still dominant size to preserve hierarchy without wrapping awkwardly.

colours.colourReason: The brand palette is derived exclusively from Techjockey brand colors. Orange becomes the primary CTA and hero emphasis color, while white and near-black define contrast and premium readability. No extra palette is introduced.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width split hero with brand/logo anchoring, large bold headline, short supporting copy, and a compact benefit list beneath; primary emphasis is on immediate readability and conversion rather than storytelling.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single dominant hero followed by a lead-capture/form block and then stacked content sections; rhythm is linear, top-heavy, and form-forward with limited narrative branching.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple utility cards/blocks with strong borders or subtle elevation, minimal ornament, and dense information hierarchy; content is organized for scanning rather than visual exploration.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA appears as a prominent action label in the hero and/or within each product section; CTA strategy is direct and repeated, with low emphasis on secondary actions.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module is evident in the provided structure.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not present in the provided excerpt; footer behavior cannot be confirmed.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media use in the visible structure; logo placement is prominent while large illustrative panels are absent in the excerpt; any media is likely supporting rather than immersive.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked product-detail sections with a label, headline, descriptive paragraph, and a feature list; each section functions like a modular information block with repeated structure.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form block directly below the hero, using a card container, headline, and multiple hidden fields for tracking/qualification; high-conversion form placement is a primary pattern.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit animation pattern is evidenced in the provided markup; structure suggests a static, utility-led landing page.
designNotes: Prioritize conversion-first hierarchy: logo, headline, benefits, then form.
Use compact copy blocks and dense information grouping for professional B2B audiences.
Keep component styling restrained and utility-focused; avoid decorative UI.
Repeat section structure to compare offerings quickly.
If expanded, consider adding a strong contrast change only where it supports scannability, not ornament.

Pricing or quote blocks positioned as decision support rather than upfront friction
Testimonial section from creative and marketing roles to validate enterprise use cases

avoidPatterns: Avoid long editorial storytelling before showing product outputs
Avoid badge-only trust without logo visibility
Avoid overly decorative or experimental layouts that reduce scanability
Avoid burying video gallery content below the fold
Avoid weak or ambiguous CTA labels
Avoid dense paragraphs that obscure model capabilities
designStrategy.reasoning: This page should convert professionals who already understand the category and are evaluating capable AI visual tools. The strongest strategy is product-led with immediate proof, using logos as the primary trust cue because the instructions explicitly prioritize them. A split hero gives enough space for headline clarity and direct CTA pressure while keeping the product message visible. The second fold should be a rich video gallery because Seedance 1.5 Pro needs visual demonstration to build confidence quickly. The layout should stay balanced and scan-friendly, with repeated conversion moments and concise feature blocks that support evaluation without overwhelming the user.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
